summary: How the Parrot sample sets up Enhanced Input (Input Actions, IMC_Gameplay, triggers, dead-zone modifiers), adds the mapping context in BP_ParrotPlayerController, and builds a runtime key-remapping screen with Common UI that saves bindings to disk.
keys: Edit > Project Settings > Engine > Enhanced Input
gotchas: Runtime input remapping is still experimental; use caution shipping it
Notify User Settings must be true on Add Mapping Context for remapping to work
Player Mappable Key Settings Name must be unique across all input actions
Mapping contexts are evaluated by priority, so set it carefully when layering

summary: Maps Unity GameObjects, components and Update() to Unreal UObjects, Actors, Actor/Scene/Primitive Components and Tick(), and lists the key Gameplay Framework classes (Pawn, Character, Controller, Game Mode, Game State, Data Asset).
gotchas: Actors tick by default; component TickComponent() is disabled by default
Prefer components over child Actors for hierarchy to reduce performance and memory cost

summary: Hub page for a Maya-user tutorial series: install and set up a project, animate a Control Rig prop in Sequencer, add lighting, and render with the Movie Render Pipeline.

First-time guide to the Epic Games Developer Portal for subscription licensees: sign-in with 2FA, creating an organization, assigning tool seats, Dashboard/Organization/Purchases pages, and a seat-licensing FAQ.
gotchas: Every member needs an Epic Games account with two-factor authentication
Members must accept the organization invite before seats can be assigned
Seats are per-person; no floating licenses

summary: Recommended and minimum hardware/OS, IDE (Visual Studio, Xcode, clang) and driver requirements for UE5 on Windows, macOS and Linux, plus the GPU/OS/SM6 requirements for Lumen, MegaLights, Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps, TSR and Path Tracing.
gotchas: Lumen, MegaLights and Nanite/VSM need SM6 enabled in Project Settings; Lumen needs NVIDIA RTX-2000+ / AMD RX-6000+ / Intel Arc
Lumen Hardware Ray Tracing requires SM6 set in Project Settings
Use Visual Studio 2026 for general development; 2022 only for Nintendo/older AGDE
Xcode 26.4 is not compatible with Unreal Engine

summary: Tutorial step for adding and tweaking Directional, Point, Spot and Rect lights and Exponential Height Fog, placing a Cine Camera and keyframing it in Sequencer, and using a Post Process Volume or camera post-process settings.
gotchas: Camera post-process settings are only visible when piloting that camera or rendering from it in Sequencer
Right Ctrl + L and drag rotates the Directional Light

summary: Tutorial step: create an Open World level and a Level Sequence, drag in the CR_Cardbox Control Rig, use Animation mode, keyframe proxy/global/squash-stretch controls, and refine keys with the Curve Editor and Tween Tools.
gotchas: Requires the Control Rig Sample Pack from Fab
Ctrl + ` toggles world/local space for rotating multiple controls

summary: Outlines the three Movie Render Pipeline tools (Movie Render Graph, Movie Render Queue, Quick Render) and walks through Sequencer's Quick Render button using the legacy Movie Scene Capture to export a video or image sequence.
gotchas: Movie Render Queue is a plugin that must be enabled for the project
Movie Scene Capture is the legacy tool with minimal settings

summary: Import methods, supported file formats (FBX, OBJ, USD, Alembic, texture formats, IES) and Maya export/import checklists for static and skeletal meshes: units, Z-up axes, pivots at origin, UVs, LODs, Nanite and morph targets.
gotchas: Unreal uses centimeters, left-handed, Z-up coordinates
Pivot comes from the world origin on export; offset geometry gets an offset pivot
Baked lighting needs non-overlapping UVs or artifacts appear
Import the skeletal mesh first without animation, then import animations separately against its skeleton

summary: Installs Unreal Engine via the Epic Games Launcher, creates a Third Person template project from the Project Browser, and adds the Control Rig Sample Pack from Fab inside the editor.

Walks through each stage of Unreal's deferred rendering pipeline (culling, depth pass, draw calls, GBuffer, texture streaming, materials, reflections, static and Lumen lighting, fog/translucency, post-process and TSR) with the Unity equivalent for each.
gotchas: Textures need power-of-2 sizes to get mipmaps
Lumen replaces Screen Space Reflections when used
TSR runs after depth of field; later effects such as motion blur and bloom are upscaled

summary: Overview for Maya users of Lumen GI, Virtual Shadow Maps, light types and their Maya equivalents, Post Process Volumes, the Light Mixer, Color Grading and Environment Light Mixer panels, and the Day Sequence time-of-day plugin.
gotchas: Maximum of two Directional Lights, each needing a different Atmosphere Sun Light Index
HDRIs on a Sky Light need Real Time Capture enabled
Virtual Shadow Maps are on by default in DirectX 12 projects

summary: Step-by-step export from Unity and import into Unreal for static meshes, skeletal meshes, animations, textures, materials, audio, video and 2D sprites, with FBX import options and fixes for scale and rotation problems; also maps Unity VFX Graph, Timeline and C# to Niagara, Sequencer and C++/Blueprint.
gotchas: Unreal's FBX pipeline uses FBX 2020.2; use that version to avoid incompatibilities
1 Unreal unit = 1 cm vs Unity's 1 m, so imports may come in too small
A 90.0 X-axis Import Rotation fixes Unity-to-Unreal rotation issues
Shader Graph, VFX Graph, Timeline/Cinemachine and C# scripts cannot be imported and must be rebuilt

summary: Onboarding guide for subscription licensees: Developer Portal and Epic Pro Support access, account 2FA, system requirements, ways to get the engine (Launcher, offline installer, distributed install, GitHub, Perforce), Datasmith setup, launching the editor and creating projects.
gotchas: Console development needs a source build, not the Launcher binary
Offline installation limits Fab access
Only one authorized user may log into the Perforce account
XInput, X3DAudio and XAudio are not in standard DirectX installs and must be installed or shipped

summary: How the Parrot 2.5D platformer camera works: UParrotCameraSubsystem reads per-map settings from AParrotWorldSettings, and AParrotCamera supports None, Fixed and Follow modes using a trigger box and a blocking mesh that stops backward movement.

Hub page for the Parrot Game Sample, a free pirate 2.5D platformer built in both UE 5.6 and Unity 6; links to its pages on Level Blueprints, subsystems, serialization, gameplay framework, characters, cameras, enemies, combat, triggers, Sequencer, UI, Enhanced Input and audio.

Parrot's player setup: importing an FBX character, the generated Skeleton/Skeletal Mesh/Physics Asset, building an Animation Blueprint, the AParrotCharacterBase/AParrotPlayerCharacter C++ classes, a Blueprint player controller using Enhanced Input, and a custom UParrotCharacterMovementComponent for platformer jumps.
gotchas: Only one Physics Asset per Skeletal Mesh
Put input handling in the player controller once behavior gets complex, because pawns are transient
The map needs a PlayerStart actor and a viewable camera to test

summary: Overview of Unreal scripting options: editor-only Python (with links to Control Rig, Sequencer, IK Rig and IK Retargeter Python pages), Blueprint types, Animation Blueprints, Editor Utility Widgets, and the Scriptable Tools system.
gotchas: Python works only in the editor and cannot be used for runtime scripting
Scriptable Tools are modal: no other tool can be active while one is in use

summary: How Parrot saves player settings by subclassing UGameUserSettings (UParrotGameUserSettings) for volume values, set through the Game User Settings Class project setting; also mentions SaveGame objects for simple saves.
keys: Edit > Project Settings > Engine - General Settings
gotchas: The Game User Settings Class must point to your subclass or it will not be used

summary: Explains Unreal subsystems (Engine, Editor, Game Instance, World, Local Player scopes) as a managed-lifetime alternative to Unity singletons, using Parrot's Game Instance-scoped UParrotAudioSubsystem as the example.

Short Unity-to-Unreal FAQ: auto-loading the last project, where input bindings and the startup level are set, ways to run the game, cm units and axes, Output Log, check()/ensure() instead of exceptions, .NET containers vs TArray/TMap/TSet, and hot reload.
keys: Always Load Last Project on Startup
gotchas: Unreal does not use exceptions; check() halts and ensure() logs with a call stack and continues
Unreal units are centimeters, not meters

summary: Maps the Unity editor to Unreal Editor (Outliner, Details, Content Browser, Output Log, menus, viewport), plus Project Settings, Plugins, levels and World Settings, default map, Actors/components vs prefabs, and packaging through the Platforms dropdown.
gotchas: Screenshots and terms are from UE 5.4.3

summary: Hub for Maya users: contrasts real-time Unreal pipelines with offline Maya ones, gives a Maya-to-Unreal terminology table (Hypershade = Material Editor, Graph Editor = Curve Editor, etc.), and links the topic pages.

Parrot's audio setup: importing audio, sound cues, a MainSoundClass with Music/SFX children and DefaultSoundMix, Play Sound 2D for pickups, looping music, runtime volume changes via sound mix overrides, and a C++ UParrotAudioSubsystem that picks music per map.
gotchas: Set music virtualization to Play When Silent, or muting destroys the sound and it won't resume
Supported imports: .wav, .ogg, .flac, .aif, .opus, .mp3 at 16 or 24 bit; stored internally as 16-bit uncompressed wav

summary: Hub page for Maya users moving to Unreal; links to the editor/features overview and the getting-started animating guide.

Hub page for Unity developers; links to the Unity-to-Unreal overview, asset migration, rendering intro, 2D, Blueprint vs C++, game objects, writing code, gameplay examples, systems overview, FAQ and the Parrot sample.

Parrot's Game Mode (BP_ParrotGameMode), C++/Blueprint Game State and Game Instance classes, how they are set in Maps & Modes, and level loading via UParrotMapDataAsset soft references with Async Load Asset, Open Level and CommonLoadingScreen.
gotchas: The game mode can be overridden per map (Parrot's main menu uses a different one)
Update the game mode and game state as new classes are created
